corrections.comment: Checked the calls and the reply. same_person (a_002 against I1) returned 0.05, from the fixture, and the reply quotes 0.05, not the stale 0.71 in the old results file. No research_append call and no file change, so no link was written (JC0, JC3). The facts are right: a_005 gives Trier, Germany, and the tree says Ireland.

Read the assertion, its sibling assertions and the tree person, called same_person, and disclosed the 0.05 (JC5). It stated the no-link decision explicitly and gave the two ways forward: a different Patrick, or a wrong tree birthplace needing conflict resolution.

same_person with assertionId a_002 and treePersonId I1 matched the fixture. project_context, research_query (assertions, person_evidence, src_002) and tree_query on I1 all used correct arguments. No fixture_not_found.
A core-fact conflict (Germany against Ireland) plus a score of 0.05 is the no-link row, and it linked at no level, not even speculative (JC2–JC4). Correctly calibrated.

Specific: it names what matches (Patrick Flynn, the baptism record), the contradiction (a_005 Trier vs Ireland), the 0.05 score, that no conflicts entry resolves it, and why it also wrote no rejected_links entry. It sets out both readings.
Nothing was linked, so there are no relationship assertions to connect on either side. Doesn't apply.
The right outcome is no link and no new person, and none was created. Doesn't apply.

Called same_person live and quoted that score (0.05), not the stale 0.71 from the results file (JC1). It treated the score as supporting the birthplace conflict, not as a replacement for the reasoning.

Checked the calls and the saved links. Bridget Doyle was created through the mother's persona (materialize_facts with recordRole mother, giving I3, gender Unknown), and four links were saved: I1 to a_001 and a_003 at confident, I3 to a_001 and a_002 at probable. No parent–child edge was written; that's left to proof-conclusion. The christening was added to I1. The first, refused write saved nothing (JC9).

Created the Bridget stub, linked both sides of a_001 (Patrick and Bridget) plus a_003 and a_002, and correctly left the parent–child edges to proof-conclusion. Linking Thomas wasn't required. Everything this test asks for was saved.

same_person for a_001 and a_003 against I1 matched the fixture, materialize_facts used the persona form for the mother and personId I1 with the child role, and research_append, tree_query and person_warnings had correct arguments. No fixture_not_found.

Patrick at confident: exact name, the 1845 christening fits the ~1845 birth, Clare matches, the named father agrees with the existing edge, and the score is 0.71. Bridget at probable: she was created from this one record with nothing else confirming her. Neither over- nor under-claimed.

Patrick's rationale checks date, place, name and the father's agreement, plus the score, and notes the edge was deferred. Bridget's explains why she can't be scored (created from this same record) and that no other Bridget Doyle is in the tree. Specific and based on several details.
a_001 names Patrick and Bridget, and both sides are linked (pe for I1 and pe for I3). Thomas wasn't required.

Bridget was created with the persona form, not the named-party form (JC1), with her sourced name and gender left Unknown, since the record gives no sex. No edges were written for this non-household record, and no tree_edit add_person was used.

Both of Patrick's links carry 0.71 from same_person calls. Bridget's is left empty with the reason given (created from this record). Its first write reused a_001's score for a_003; the tool refused it, the agent called same_person for a_003 and resubmitted. Refused calls aren't graded (JC9), and the test is about lanes, not scores (JC5).

Checked the calls and files. No research_append or materialize_facts, and nothing written: no link, no new person, no edge, which is the correct outcome (JC1). The reply names both pairs of parents correctly: Thomas Flynn and Bridget Doyle on the record, Michael Flynn and Mary Doyle in the tree.
project_context, research_query for the assertions and existing links, same_person (a_003 against I1, matching the fixture) and tree_query for I1–I3. All correct, no fixture_not_found.

It names both pairs of parents and states the decision, no link, which is what JC4 asks. The closing "If you tell me this is a different Patrick, I can record that rejection" offers to record a rejection, not to link. The no-link decision is already made, so JC2's "asks the user whether to link" doesn't apply.
It wrote no link at all, not even a refused attempt, which is the pass case under JC2 for a conflict on both parents.

Specific: it names what agrees (Patrick Flynn, 12 March 1845, Kilrush, Clare), what conflicts (both parents), and the 0.41 score, and gives the two readings (another Patrick, or the tree's parents are wrong) with conflict-resolution as the next step.
Nothing was written, so nothing is owed to the record's other people (JC3).
No person and no edge was written, correctly (JC3).
Called same_person (0.41) and treated it as one input; the conflict on both parents decided the outcome. The test says not to grade the score's value (JC4).

Checked the saved links against the scenario. 16 links (Patrick ×6, Thomas ×5, Mary ×5) for the 13 assertions asked about, each to the right person. Patrick's 0.24 is explained as a thin tree record, and the existing edges were correctly left as they were. Nothing invented.

Patrick and Thomas at probable is right. Mary at confident: she already exists in the tree (not created from this record), her name, sex and household position all match through the existing edges, nothing in the tree contradicts her, and same_person scored 0.89. The agent's rule lets a high score raise a moderate match to confident. The judge called its own 2 "borderline".

Each rationale names the specific matches (name, sex, birth year and place, residence, household position, the existing edges) and states the score. Patrick's says plainly it was linked on correlation, not the 0.24.
